name: Rooted Factors Can Have Non-Ample Sink Sets
statement: There is an ample rooted factor $(S,0)$ with $870$ concepts and isometric dimension $14$ such that $\operatorname{Sink}(S)$ is not isometric and hence not ample. In its integer encoding, $1,2\in\operatorname{Sink}(S)$ while $0,3\notin\operatorname{Sink}(S)$.
proof: The stored construction and all 28 rooted elementary-minor orders certify that $(S,0)$ is a rooted factor. Two explicit complete corner orders end at 2 and 1. Rooted failure excludes 0; restricting any hypothetical order ending at 3 to the terminal core face would make the normalized core peel to its forbidden root. Vertices 1 and 2 are at Hamming distance two, and their only ambient common neighbours are precisely the two excluded vertices, so the induced sink graph is not isometric.
